[b]The word does not become flesh | [sub]Stormhaven | ██ March 2025[/sub][/b]

A small black van was driving along the highway leading into the Stormhaven Metropolis. The engine hummed silently, permeating through the industrial ether, never quite loud enough to be distinguishable from the midnight noise, never quite overt sufficient to be trackable by cameras or by naked eyes. The dark tinted windows that shrouded the van's interior ensured its secrecy even as it passed by the luminous Dyrssen Tower or magnificent Ipsen Hall, nor was it ever the object of gossip or discussion by the beleaguered crowds who'd sooner lambast the rundown station wagon that trailed behind it or praise the fine GTs and supercars that would make their home on that busy Stormhaven intersection.

Red light. The van stopped. The driver blinked once, twice, thrice. He stared impatiently at the traffic light, then turned his head from side to side as if in search of something that wasn't there. Green light. The van continues along the dark asphalt, relishing for a moment in the decadent Stormhaven lights before retreating down an intersection into the industrial jungle of the city outskirts. The driver continues along the darkening until halting beneath the shadow of a hotel ruin, the so-called Palace of Dreams, which towered ominously over downtown Stormhaven as a reminder of the city's quieter days.

Two figures step out of the van. The first, the driver, is featureless because of his face mask. His passenger, better dressed and less capable of obscuring his trademark glasses and rich black hair, was Xavier Almstedt. 

He stood beneath the shadow of the Palace of Dreams for a minute and leaned against the van, chuckling to himself as he hummed to the tune of the muffled screams ensconced within. He raised his head to his forehead in a shielding gaze from the bright lights of the Palace as its front doors opened, revealing two figures exiting. Leading of the two was the slim figure of a woman in fine executive dress. Her sharp and piercing gaze easily gave away her identity. It was Alice Ostman, the Minister of Foreign Affairs. Next to her was a heavily armed paramilitary escort from an uncertain organization.

The driver remained silent as Ostman approached the van, his head kept low and humble, while Xavier would be much more forthcoming, his eyes lighting up like the stars as he raised his hand in an enthusiastic wave. Ostman is unimpressed by the crude display.

[list]

"Hey, Minister Ostman!" Xavier yelled out, much to the Minister's chagrin. "Awesome work on the island, by the way. Manhandled those Thrømm pricks real well, I was watching your speech over the news and everything! Porthwaite's board wants to thank you. Hell, the country thanks you!"

"Whatever." Ostman flatly rebuffed.

"... Huh, what's gotten you all pissed off? I'm being serious here. This is like, a new beginning for High Albany! We're no longer just a bunch of quiet industrialists anymore. With our acquisition of Austmark, we've proven to the rest of Erene that High Albany can put its foot down when others try to take what is ours. I mean damn, I'm feeling all giddy just thinking about it. Do you feel it too, Minister?"

[/list]

Xavier walks over to the Foreign Minister's side and gives her arm a nudge with her elbow, though she shows little reciprocation. 

[list]

"Leave me out of your fantasies, Almstedt," Ostman replied as she crossed her arms. "Gloating is an invitation to bitter irony. Anyways, I've done my part, so where is the whistleblower?"

"Heh, impatient..."

[/list]

Backing off, Xavier chuckled as he turned to the driver, who nodded to the signal and walked around to the back of the van. Opening the rear doors, he grabs hold of a man bound tightly by layers of rope. The man was clearly in his younger years and involved in academia judging by his damaged lanyard, perhaps a graduate student or even a teaching assistant. He was in a sorry state, unable to keep one eye open from a terrible bruise, and unable to move his legs from a similar dilemma. A thin film of translucent greenish-white cream is visible, perhaps a topical ointment, haphazardly placed all over his injuries as a crude manner of treatment. Minister Ostman inspected the man carefully, glossing over his damaged form, squinting, then sighing.

[list]

"Mmf... mmmm...!" The man attempted to scream out in protest through his gagged mouth.

 "... Mr. Almstedt..." Ostman began, looking bemused. "Why does he have so many bruises? I said I wanted him unscathed. You think I just pluck good coroners out of the ocean?"

"Yeah, well, we had a bit of trouble escorting him out of the dorm and all," Xavier replied sheepishly. "We did apply a bit of ointment so he could heal up better but like, if you want to keep him alive a bit longer..."

"Ugh... it's fine, we'll just turn him into ivory like the last one..." Ostman bemoaned, reaching out to carefully grasp at the man's cheekbones, turning him to face her in the eyes. Then, she let go. "... Anyway, thank you Mr. Almstedt. You've done your country proud. Now, get the hell out of here before we get photographed."

"Alright, alright, have fun with that prick. Happy doing business!"

[/list]

Xavier tipped his head sardonically to the Minister and the unfortunate soul resting at her feet before turning around to the van. He had a visible spring in his step as he patted the driver on the shoulder for a job well done as the two entered the van, with Xavier giving the Minister one last cheery glance before backing out of the Palace of Dreams and away from that sordid meeting. Ostman turned to her escort, who would nod and grab hold of the man, slinging him over their shoulder.

There was a blur in time.

Then, the man woke up. There was not a slick of sweat on his skin, for the air conditioner blared loudly overhead. He was still tied to that chair, bound on his legs and on his arms. Surrounding the man were half a dozen military-aged men and women, wearing fine black armor non-standard to those used by the Commonwealth armed forces. No, they were not soldiers of the state but mercenaries. Printed proudly across their chest were the tags of their corporation: "SummitONE Solutions", Xavier Almstedt's company.

The Minister crouched down beside him, her voice lowering to something almost gentle. It really is a shame, she murmured. A smart man like you should've known to keep their head down low on political matters.

The journalist flinched, his body tightening against the ropes. A muffled, desperate plea barely escaped his gag. His one good eye darted between Ostman and the masked escort, sweat forming along his temple.

[list]

Right, the gag... she continued, brushing a loose strand of hair from his bloodied forehead. Keith Talfourd. You've been such a frustrating thorn in our side for upwards " Emanating from beyond the mass of mercs was Minister Ostman, who had been watching over the man's condition from the shadows. "Pardon the rough treatment, I didn't anticipate that Almstedt would be so sloppy as to bruise you up for such a basic mission."

"Argh... hah..." Keith took a moment to catch his breath. Then, raising his head, he responded, his words "Whatever, fed... So what? I'm dead now? Because I decided to do the right thing?"

"Call it what you want." The Minister smirked and walked past her troops, then stared down at the pitiful activist in front of her. "What the Commonwealth needs are strong leaders, and I am strong. We give the people sanctuary and stability. Student activists skittering around like rats undermine both the people and their leaders."

"YOU'RE the one who's calling it what you want!" he shouted back, gazing fiercely at the Minister. "You think killing me is gonna solve anything? Half the state already knows about the Mailliard report!"

The Minister raised her left eyebrow but otherwise kept her expression stoic. "I resigned before the Mailliard report became public. My name isn't on it. How interesting it is that a student of all people could manage to sniff me out of that mess of a document... 

"Students spend all their time wasting away in academia; you think it's weird that one of us managed to find you out?" Keith says, smirking ever so slightly. "I know that you had friends in that report, Ostman... I know that you protected those friends... and hell, I've spoken to the reporters. My name is tied to your name now... but if you free me, I can make a retraction, we can put this whole thing behind u-... argh!"

[/list]

Keith's words are cut short by a loud thud. It was the sound of Ostman's heel digging deep into the student's shin. Bone against bone, crunching, tearing, shifting. The Minister released her hold on the student, who crumpled into his seat, though in between bated breaths, he would continue gazing defiantly at Ostman when he could.

"And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us." Ostman flatly said, talking down to him. "You're a bona fide idiot, Talfourd. What is said comes into existence; there is no unmaking but through Monad's intercession. As long as you implant an idea in the minds of men it shall will itself into existence. It doesn't matter if you whisper quietly and tell the right people because there are no right people in this world. No good reporters especially." Ostman lowered her voice and crossed her arms, stepping away from Keith. "But it's alright, Mr. Talfourd... I forgive you... I forgive you because this grave sin which I've described has not come to pass yet. Celice, Cassidy, Barnatt, Donarum, Sumner... these were the reporters, correct?"

Keith widened his eyes as each name exited from the Minister's breath. It was the names of every reporter he ever contacted. Every single one, even those who swiftly hung up his calls to stave off controversy, even those who refused to pick up for fear of their own families. "You..." Keith spoke quietly, struggling to get the words out. "You... killed them...?"

"For legal reasons, no," Ostman said, matter-of-factly. "They just collectively decided to go off-the-grid and live as a far-left commune somewhere in the Hollows where they ended up getting gored to death by moose. It's wonderful that you only contacted journalists who were already under surveillance, who lived like hermits in their little nests, paranoid and waiting for when the day will come. We could've killed you long ago too." She remarked, tilting her head mockingly at Keith. "...but you were too high-profile to be more convenient dead."

"You're insane..." Keith quipped, appalled. "Y-You're completely deranged..." 

"I am of perfectly sound mind, Mr. Talfourd." The Minister replied candidly. "We know everything about you not because we want to, but because we need to. Homeland Security makes sure we keep a tight leash on any potential subversives. We give you the sort of freedom that rests on the parameter that we have demarcated. The people accept this freedom because the ruins of lost civilizations quietly remind us what happens if we were to let people step out of line."

"And what happens after I die, huh Ostman? My family will come looking for me... the press, I've been interviewed more than a hundred times already... they know that I've been keeping dirt on you and all the other White Sea mafiosi..." Keith struggled against his bindings once more, then forcibly jerked himself forward, shifting his chair closer and closer to the Minister. "I'm still gonna be in your head even when I'm gone! You do understand that, don't you?!"

But there was no reaction. Ostman stood coolly, her countenance never once failing.

"Anathema honors anathema..." she began, "... but everyone in High Albany or on Erene will not care for you. Do you not understand? Men seek shelter in what's good enough. They fear losing what they have in wagering for what could be better. Your name will be forgotten, Mr. Talfourd. It's actively being forgotten from the moment you woke up in that chair. There can be no freedom fighters in a free world."

[list]

"Do I look like a free man to you? Bound in ropes and waiting for his death at a fed's hand?"

"When you try to usurp the freedom of any person or state, they will be privy to usurp you too," Ostman responded. "So rejoice, Mr. Talfourd, because there is nothing left for you here. Do you think history will honor your death with a eulogy?"

[/list]

 The Minister's voice cut through the still air like a blade.

[b]STORMHAVEN METROPOLITAN POLICE INVESTIGATE MISSING JOURNALIST[/b]

[list]

STORMHAVENThe Metropolitan Police have opened an investigation into the disappearance of an independent journalist last seen near his university residence earlier this week. The individual, known for reporting on political affairs and government transparency, failed to appear for a scheduled interview with the [i]Stormhaven Tribune[/i], raising concerns among colleagues and close contacts.

Law enforcement sources confirm that surveillance footage from the universitys northern sector has been retrieved for examination, though no official leads have been disclosed. A police spokesperson stated that while no signs of foul play have been identified, authorities remain vigilant and encourage anyone with relevant information to come forward.

The case has sparked discussions regarding the safety of investigative reporters in High Albany, particularly in light of recent claims concerning national security matters. However, government officials have dismissed allegations of state involvement, calling such speculation sensationalism.

More updates will follow as the investigation continues.[/list]

[nation]High Albany[/nation]

[b]The Hall of Columns (Presidential Palace):  March 6th, 2025[/b]

Theodora rarely saw her son, he was a strong and independent politician who tended to distance himself from the dramas and intrigues which surrounded the president and the first lady, preferring to work with the politicians and not the dynastic nobility. 

Nevertheless she had successfully managed to gain some time with him the afternoon following the successful vote in the Chamber of the Peoples.

As they walked along the great hall of columns, a massive hall that ran from the main entrance of the residence to the inner garden courtyard, Theodora and Consantin VII chatted casually.

How is your wife? enquired Theodora, opening the conversation with ease.

Eudoxia is fine, shes been taking care of our son at the country home, hes a boisterous young lad Ill give you tha, replied Consantin.

That is lovely to hear, I do hope she considers visiting us sometime, replied Theodora in a lilting motherly tone. 

Eudoxia had not visited the family since Consantin had been sworn into the Chamber of the Peoples, fearing the machinations of the realpolitik  machine in the capital she had reserved herself and the two children of Consantin to the countryside, away from the hustle and bustle of the capital. 

Well you know how she feels about the city, replied Consantin in a knowing tone.

Oh hum, well perhaps I can go to her, replied Theodora smiling.

You know wed love to host you, stated Consantin, stopping to admire a mosaic that was displayed on one of the walls, it depicted the final stages of the revolution of 64 that had led to the full independence of North Thýven, a heroic piece that reeked of pride and nationalism. 

You did a good job yesterday with the coalition, intoned Theodora, looking up at the mosaic.

How did you know? enquired Consantin.

Theodora looked at her son with surprise, Did I not raise you? I know my son's deeds because I know his mind, she replied laughing slightly, in reality Jænus Albringer had reported the matter to her before she left the basilica after her tumultuous meeting with Alexander Mekedii. 

Consantin remained silent for a few moments before turning to continue walking, Do tell me mother, why did you call me here, surely it wasnt just for chit chat, he stated finally getting to the point.

I visited Senator Mekedii yesterday, replied Theodora.

Ah, so you WERE in the basilica, I  had heard a small whisper, replied Consantin knowingly.

That I do not deny, but, anyways, I visited the man yesterday and gave him an offer, an offer which he rejected unfortunately, Continued Theodora.

Is that so? What did you offer him? enquired Consantin.

The speakership of the Senate, replied Theodora bluntly.

Consantin frowned, his mother had no right to be touching the institutions that were constitutionally enshrined to protect the people from the tyranny of the presidency. His mother picking up on the frown pierced through his thoughts, saying, No need to look so gruff, I have always done this, you are fully aware of this, she stated calmly.

It doesnt make it right, replied Consantin, There are better ways to make deals, such as coalitioning, he continued.

Yes, but wheres the fun in that? joked Theodora laughing slightly, but I digress, no, I was quite upset that Mekedii turned down my offer, it was a good offer, she stated.

Do tell me, why did you offer him the position? enquired Consantin.

Because Tito is weak, he must be removed, he makes our position too obvious, replied Theodora coldly.

Consantin nodded thoughtfully, Well what next? Your offer failed, what shall you do next? he enquired after a moment's silence.

You will know when you see it, replied Theodora, I still have to make sure of the details, she continued. 

The two continued walking on the discussion shifting from politics to loose and casual everyday things, yet Consantin worried what his mother might do next, she was known to be quite a strategist and even he was not blind to that.

[b]The Shamat Gambit | [sub]Covert | 17 March 2025[/sub][/b]

A certain phone call was made and a certain gentleman's agreement had been reached.

In the great blue skies of Erene, a lone black transport aircraft was seen, quietly enveloped in a blanket of great clouds. It was no passenger plane but a turbopop military airlift, officially designated as the Springflame-4A. While unmarked to avoid the scrutiny of international powers, the aircraft was a corporate unit of SummitONE Solutions, a shadowy private military company and subsidiary of Norrhollow's Almstedt Corporation.

After flying over the featureless Baliwick Sea for hours on end, the Springflame would pass over the southwestern peninsula of West Shamat, passing by Imperio Joanesko and Chechnya and finally reaching Sal-Baliz. A lone white light would be shone over the airport at Aduab to signal the aircraft's friendly intentions.

The plane would land on the asphalt without incident, then shutting down. The door of the Springflame opens, and men in heavy military gear would walk out, covered head-to-toe as if to obscure their identities, though in the midst of it a clear label would be clearly marked on their body armor, proudly displaying their corporate allegiance:

SummitONE Solutions.

[nation]Sal-Baliz[/nation]
